links.measurement_definition: Defendant not released within three days of bail hearing; study treatment is the complementary binary release indicator.
links.units: 0/1 per defendant; aggregate denominator would be defendants with bail hearings
links.recorded_producer_or_source_data: Administrative court bail-hearing and jail-release records. Existing src/simulation/justice/pretrial.ts and prosecution.ts decide individual cases; inventory explicitly says place-rate application would double count. No place aggregate or new producer established by this research.
links.outcome_definition: Found guilty of any offense at disposition; guilty pleas separately recorded.
links.source_horizon: Case disposition; fixed month lag not established by opened material
unknowns: Opened Harvard working-paper version reports 15.6 percentage-point release effect; do not silently replace final-paper coefficient or treat inventory 0.24–0.35 as a confidence interval.
Do not use a place detention rate to decide a defendant.

links.outcome_definition: Formal employment is positive annual W-2 earnings.
links.source_horizon: First two full years and third/fourth full years after bail; cited long-run result is years 3–4
unknowns: Six-month inventory lag is not the measured long-run horizon.
A 25% default spread is not a source confidence interval.

links.measurement_definition: Recorded enactment and effective date of reclassification of specified lower-level drug/property offenses under Proposition 47.
links.units: 0/1 law-in-force indicator, with offense-specific statutory scope
links.recorded_producer_or_source_data: Law record must encode which offenses and penalties changed; California DOJ statewide crime/arrest data and BSCC–PPIC records supply observed outcomes. Inventory says no shipped reclassification question/reader.
unknowns: 9% / 135 per 100,000 is an estimate, not a numeric interval.
Inventory contested range 0–0.18 is a default, not PPIC uncertainty.
Policy bundling means generic release is not the measured cause.

links.measurement_definition: County exposed to hurricane-strength winds within estimated maximum-wind-speed radius; hurricane cutoff 74 mph.
links.units: County-storm exposure 0/1; wind mph, storm location and six-hour observations
links.recorded_producer_or_source_data: National Hurricane Center HURDAT2 storm tracks/wind/pressure plus Extended Best Track maximum-wind radius; BEA county transfers measure outcome. Inventory reports no per-place disaster reader.
links.outcome_definition: Additional non-disaster social-insurance transfers per resident, present value in 2013 dollars.
links.source_horizon: 1979–2002 storms, 1969–2012 outcomes; ten years after hurricane

source_reported_range.units: 2013 dollars per capita present value over ten post-storm years
source_reported_range.kind: range of estimates, not annual rate

unknowns: Generic severe disaster is not the study treatment.
Annual proportional conversion and baseline in inventory are repository derivations, not primary-source coefficients.

packets.scope: Last 9 of 19 cause-not-recorded links, positions 11–19 in filtered file order; research only

primarySource.title: Aizer et al. (2018), Do Low Levels of Blood Lead Reduce Children's Future Test Scores?

measurement.definition: Average preschool blood lead linked to third-grade reading; substantially-below-proficient reading is a separate outcome.
measurement.units: Blood lead: micrograms per deciliter; reading: share/percentage points.

links.recordedProducerOrSourceData: Study links individual preschool blood lead measurements to third-grade tests for Rhode Island birth cohorts. Clinical blood-test records are the relevant cause record; a tested-child elevated-lead share does not supply mean blood lead.
links.sourceHorizon: Preschool exposure to third grade; birth cohorts 1997–2005. Exact 48-month lag not verified from opened abstract.
researchGaps: No representative state mean or 56-place coverage established. Full methods blocked by paywall/PMC access check. No empirical interval verified.
findings: Published abstract reports 0.96 percentage-point reading change per one-unit decrease; catalog 3.1-point IV anchor is not verified by this abstract.

additionalSources.finding: CDC 2017–2022 state surveillance is a tested subset, not population based; cannot compare states/counties. 2022 classifications use 3.5 micrograms/dL reference value.

links.implementation: NOT RUN; research only; no production edits or new coefficients

primarySource.title: Goodman et al., Heat and Learning, author working paper ED670816

measurement.definition: Mean daily maximum temperature on school days in the 365 days preceding PSAT; summers and weekends modeled separately.
measurement.units: Degrees Fahrenheit; alternative hot-day exposure measured as counts of school days in temperature bins.

links.recordedProducerOrSourceData: NOAA Daily Global Historical Climatology Network daily station temperatures, matched to nearest high school; College Board PSAT records and survey of classroom heat/AC.
links.sourceHorizon: Weather 1996–2014; high-school classes 2001–2014; cumulative prior-year exposure.
researchGaps: School/calendar geocoding and AC record needed. No state baseline calculated. Default catalog 25% spread is not a source interval.
links.implementation: NOT RUN; research only; no production edits or new coefficients

primarySource.title: Dettling and Kearney (2014), author university publication abstract

measurement.definition: Change in MSA-level house-price dollar level; distinguish current homeowners from non-owners.
measurement.units: US dollars per home; published comparison is $10,000 change.

links.recordedProducerOrSourceData: FHFA repeat-sales HPI can supply geographic price movement, but an index needs an independently sourced dollar-level anchor to match this measurement. Ownership must be recorded per household.
links.sourceHorizon: Abstract says short-term changes/current-period fertility; exact one-year lag not verified.
researchGaps: HPI is an index, not dollars. No price-level dataset or common territorial coverage established. Non-owners are broader than renters. No interval supplied by abstract.

additionalSources.finding: Weighted repeat-sales indexes from sales/refinancing mortgage transactions; national, state, metro, county, ZIP and tract products; history since mid-1970s.

links.implementation: NOT RUN; research only; no production edits or new coefficients

primarySource.title: Carpenter et al. (2021), Effects of Access to Legal Same-Sex Marriage on Marriage and Health

measurement.definition: Legal access to same-sex marriage in respondent state at interview date; binary policy indicator, not number of marriages.

links.recordedProducerOrSourceData: State court/legislative effective dates, matched to exact BRFSS interview date and household sex composition; canonical law effective-date record is the relevant cause.
links.sourceHorizon: BRFSS 2000–2017; adults age 25+; national access from June 2015 documented in paper.
researchGaps: Historical treatment variation does not supply present-day place variation. Same-sex household proxy is not all sexual-minority men; population conversion requires separate denominator evidence. No aggregate uninsured effect interval verified.
findings: Final paper insurance effect is 4.1 percentage points among men in same-sex households; women results inconclusive. Catalog says 4.2 and 2000–2016.
links.implementation: NOT RUN; research only; no production edits or new coefficients

primarySource.title: Miller, Wherry and Foster (2023), The Economic Consequences of Being Denied an Abortion

measurement.definition: Woman seeking wanted abortion denied because pregnancy exceeds facility gestational limit; distinguish just-below-limit receipt comparison group.
measurement.units: Person-level denial indicator; gestational age and limit in weeks; financial outcomes from credit reports.

links.recordedProducerOrSourceData: Turnaway Study encounter/denial and gestational-limit records linked to longitudinal credit reports. A law alone cannot substitute for an actual denial.
links.sourceHorizon: Ten-year financial observation period; distress persists several years after encounter.
researchGaps: Opened abstract does not define past-due debt threshold, confirm dollar denomination/year, or provide numeric interval. Full text access was paywalled; catalog 78% not independently verified here. No population denial frequency supplied.
links.implementation: NOT RUN; research only; no production edits or new coefficients

primarySource.title: Cantoni (2020), A Precinct Too Far: Turnout and Voting Costs

measurement.definition: Distance from voter location to assigned polling location, contrasting units across precinct boundaries.
measurement.units: Miles; reported one standard deviation is 0.245 mile.

links.recordedProducerOrSourceData: Election-specific voter residence and assigned polling-site locations/precinct geography could supply person-level distance (proposed record design, not a verified statewide dataset).
links.sourceHorizon: Four elections in nine municipalities in Massachusetts and Minnesota.
researchGaps: Exact road-versus-straight-line distance construction not verified from abstract. No statewide mean or 56-place baseline found. Per-mile extrapolation is not directly measured.
findings: Primary abstract gives 2–5 percent fewer ballots for 0.245-mile increase; this is study heterogeneity, not a confidence interval. Non-presidential high-minority effects three times larger.
links.implementation: NOT RUN; research only; no production edits or new coefficients

primarySource.title: Gentzkow, Shapiro and Sinkinson (2011), The Effect of Newspaper Entry and Exit on Electoral Politics

measurement.definition: Net change in number of English-language general-circulation daily newspapers headquartered in county; daily means at least four weekdays/week.
measurement.units: Count of papers per county/election-year; closure event must be recorded separately from stock.

links.recordedProducerOrSourceData: Rowell newspaper directories 1869–1876, Ayer 1880–1928, Editor and Publisher Yearbook 1932–2004; title/city/time-of-day matching produces entry/exit records.
links.sourceHorizon: Presidential-year panel 1869–2004; main estimation 1872–1928 with four-year differences.
researchGaps: Federal turnout cannot establish local-election outcome or exact 12-month lag. Modern newspaper coverage and territories unverified. Catalog range to zero/twice size is not directly reported interval.
links.implementation: NOT RUN; research only; no production edits or new coefficients

primarySource.title: Ferraz and Finan (2007 working paper; published 2008), Exposing Corrupt Politicians

measurement.definition: Publicly released municipal audit findings before an election, classified count of corruption violations; exposure timing differs from hidden misconduct.
measurement.units: Number of documented corrupt violations; public release date; incumbent reelection indicator.

links.recordedProducerOrSourceData: Brazil federal municipal audit reports plus October 2004 municipal electoral records and local-radio presence. Audit finding and dissemination records could supply this cause; allegations alone are distinct.
links.sourceHorizon: Audit reports released before versus after October 2004 municipal election.
researchGaps: Working-paper version opened; catalog specific final-paper two-violation seven-point anchor not verified. No US/56-place baseline or transferable interval. Newspaper/radio exposure requires recorded dissemination.
findings: Working paper describes nonlinear response across violation counts and possible rewards for no corruption; a universal linear penalty loses that distinction.
links.implementation: NOT RUN; research only; no production edits or new coefficients
